promptLatex: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the two results is not $7$?
hintLatex: Counting the outcomes that produce a sum of $7$ is much easier than counting all the others.
So the probability asked for is $1 - \frac{6}{36} = \frac{5}{6}$.
solutionLatex:
The sample space is the $36$ ordered pairs of faces, all equally likely.

Exactly $6$ pairs sum to $7$, namely $(1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2)$ and $(6,1)$, so $P(\text{sum is } 7) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}$.

The complement rule gives

$P(\text{sum is not } 7) = 1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$.
